Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
6:30 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying faster, cheaper and simpler than cash, cards or a bank transfer. You scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds.

Three main reasons:

It is free and instant. For most everyday payments there is no fee, and the money arrives straight away, at any hour and on holidays too.
It works everywhere. One app can pay a chai stall, a friend or an online shop. Small shopkeepers only need a printed QR code, with no card machine to buy.
It feels safe and easy. You share a UPI ID or phone number instead of bank details, and every payment needs your PIN. It also works in many languages, and even on basic phones.

Habit did the rest. Once your neighbours, vendors and family all use it, carrying cash feels like extra effort. Cheaper phones and mobile data, plus easy bank linking, helped it spread quickly.
